transcript: This show basically pitches itself as a reverse mean girls, where instead of going from Africa to America, Cady actually comes from America to Africa. However, I actually think that description does the show a bit of an injustice because it is not, as the title might imply, a mean girls parody or rip off. There is a Regina George-esque character and a Cady Heron-esque character, and that's kind of where the similarities stop. School girls is really a play about the pressures that beauty standards put on young girls, specifically young black girls, and the colorism that comes with it, with lighter skinned black women being far more likely to be viewed as beautiful by the rest of the world than darker skinned black women. And that's kind of part of the genius of this play. It very much lures you in with this Mean Girls premise, but then slowly starts adding to it, eventually becoming something else entirely. But by that point you're already invested in all of these characters. It's easy to see why this play was such a hit when it was first staged off Broadway. And this new Broadway production certainly does the material justice. Not only is it a stacked cast, including Denee Benton, Jasmine Amy Rogers, Patina Miller, but it also reteams director Whitney White with playwright Jocelyn Bioh. And while Whitney did not direct the original production of School Girls, she did direct Bioh's other play, Jaja's African Hair braiding Which I absolutely loved when it was on Broadway. And the two work similarly well here. They are able to balance the comedy and the drama really well, and they're able to build these worlds that feel so rich and so culturally specific, while also highlighting the universality of these stories. Now, I'm not sure if this will be considered a new play or a revival come award season. I do think this will be a strong contender in whatever category it ends up in. And School Girls or the African Mean Girls play is going to get the coveted Broadway Ben Must see Go see it! It is absolutely worth your time.
